THIS BEAD IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS WORSE THAN ITS TITLE SAYS. Not proposing a
candidate - cost.scala has my pending f849104 on it and I will not open a second overlapping change.
Asking for a ruling on sequencing at the end.

BIT-IDENTICAL. A semantic provider that abstains ENTIRELY and one that measures exactly 0.5 produce
the same cell, to the last digit:

  provider                      Semantic term   supportWeight        total
  abstains (Missing) always     Some(0.5)       0.9552238805970149   1.046875
  measures 0.5                  Some(0.5)       0.9552238805970149   1.046875
  identical = true

There is no observable difference between "the embedder had nothing to say about this pair" and
"the embedder measured a distance of 0.5". Same term, same support, same total.

AND THE AUDIT TRAIL ACTIVELY MISLEADS. The same cell reports
  missingTerms = Set(Chart, Structural, Sensory)
It names three absent terms and omits the one that was actually substituted, because `missing` is
collected only from `optional`. A reader auditing that cell sees a tidy list of what we could not
measure, and Semantic is not on it.

MECHANISM: dSem = clamp(semantic.orElse(unit, node, missingSemantic)), and orElse is
apply(...).toOption.getOrElse(default) with missingSemantic = 0.5. Semantic sits in `always`, so it
is always in `terms`, always in `eligible`, and never in `missingTerms`. Support therefore counts a
substituted constant as a measurement.

WHY THIS IS THE WORST OF THE THREE I HAVE FOUND TODAY. Chart mispriced segment cells by 14.9% and
Structural inflated chartless cells by 15%; both were latent, since WOG has no charts. This one is
different in three ways:
  1. it is TOTAL substitution, not a scaling error - the number is invented outright;
  2. it is in the HIGHEST-WEIGHTED term. semantic weight is 1.0; chart is 0.5, sensory 0.15;
  3. IT IS WIRED IN PRODUCTION TODAY. embed-bench/report.scala:283 builds
     DefaultLocalCostModel(semantic = ch.semantic, ...) and ch.semantic is the embed-core-backed
     provider from channels.scala, whose own docstring says "Abstentions stay Missing".

That last point is the sharp edge. embed-core is careful and correct - Distances.cosine refuses a
zero denominator rather than returning a number, cosineEstimate maps it to Missing(NotFinite), and
the channel docstring promises abstentions stay Missing. The promise is kept all the way to the
boundary of the cost model AND DEFEATED ONE LINE INSIDE IT. Every layer below did the honest thing
and the top layer threw it away. That is why no test caught it: each component is correct on its own
contract, and the loss happens at the seam.

Reachability is honest, not asserted: this fires whenever the embedder abstains for a unit or node -
no embedding, out-of-domain text, budget exceeded, NoSpace. Whether that happens on a given run is a
property of the embedder, but the code anticipates it explicitly, which is why MissingReason exists.
With lexicalJaccard (never abstains) nothing changes, so WOG fixtures should not move.

FIX SHAPE, and the vehicle already exists: Semantic joins the optional/eligible machinery. Absent
when the provider abstains, recorded in missingTerms, still ELIGIBLE - a semantic comparison is
possible in principle, so an abstention is a genuine missed measurement, not a dimension the cell
lacks - so support falls and the total scales honestly. If every term goes that way the cell becomes
Unassessable, which is already the right answer. missingSemantic as a silent default should go; the
same argument applies to the 0.5 imputations in dProp and dEnt, which is the rest of this bead.

This is the vision case almost verbatim: "which words support each conclusion". Here the answer is
none, and the model currently reports support 0.9552.

RULING I NEED: f849104 is pending scout re-review on cost.scala. Do I (a) wait for it to land and
then do this as its own candidate on the same bead, or (b) fold it into f849104 now? I lean (a) -
f849104 has a clean two-defect story and scout's court is reproduced in it; folding a third,
larger change in would make that review harder and would mix a no-fixture-churn change with one
that could move numbers. Say which.
